Show me the board and open the planner.

The phrase spoken in hello_board.wav, which tests/test_xr_speech_backend.py
feeds to the real faster-whisper backend in 20 ms frames.

GENERATED, NOT RECORDED — reproducible, and no real person's voice enters the
repository:

    espeak-ng -v en-us -s 140 -w raw.wav "Show me the board and open the planner."
    ffmpeg -i raw.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le hello_board.wav

16 kHz mono PCM16LE, 2.96 s, 95 KB — the wire format of the client's
AudioWorklet (docs/plans/clixr.md §10), so the test feeds this to the
transcriber exactly as the websocket will, with no resampling in between.

WHY THIS PHRASE AND NOT "hello board", which is what the filename suggests: the
first fixture said exactly that, and base.en heard "Hello Bored" — then "Hello
Bards" on a second phrasing. It is not a bug in the pipeline; "board" and
"bored" are homophones, and a bare greeting gives the model no context to
choose between them, so it picks the one that follows "hello" more often. With
the article, "the board" is unambiguous and the sentence decodes exactly. The
filename is kept because the task contract names it.

That is worth knowing beyond this fixture: it is the same failure mode §10
predicts for repo names, branch names and identifiers, reproduced on the single
most important noun in this product. Keep the typing path.

The test matches KEY WORDS case-insensitively rather than this string. A speech
model may differ on casing and punctuation between versions, and a test that
pinned those would fail an upgrade that got every word right. base.en
transcribed it exactly, punctuation included, on 2026-09-12.
